front.title: Location-Independent Evaluator Governance for Autonomous Multi-Agent Systems: Protected Appointment, Evidence-Bounded Decisions, Cross-Domain Coordination, and Separation of Execution Authority

abstract.t: Autonomous agents increasingly rely on an evaluator to review plans, evidence and outcomes before work continues, yet an evaluation result is often mistaken for permission to act. This document describes a vendor-neutral architecture in which the evaluator is a functional role, not a product: it may be a rule engine, model, program, enclave, service or human, placed locally, remotely or on a shared platform. It separates six independent lifecycles, requires a protected task-specific appointment derived from resource-owner authority, admits evidence by source, role, freshness and independence, preserves mandatory dissent, and emits typed determinations such as HOLD, DISPUTED and UNKNOWN. Its central rule is that a valid determination is not an executable authorization: separate owner-controlled authorization and a native enforcement boundary remain necessary. Twenty-seven embodiments, a threat model, data model and examiner index are provided.
